- `.+?` tries minimum but `$` requires end of string
- So `. +?` must grow to consume everything up to the last space (where ` *` can match empty)
- Actually, ` *` matches zero or more spaces, so it can match the trailing empty string after `world`
- But `. +?` is non-greedy, so it should try minimum first...

Wait, with `^(.+?) *$` on `hello world`:
1. `.+?` = `h`, check if ` *$` matches `ello world$` → ` *` matches `` (empty), but then `$` doesn't match at pos 1
2. Backtrack: `.+?` = `he`, check ` *$` on `llo world$` → same issue
3. Continue until `.+?` = `hello world`, then ` *` matches `` (empty at end), `$` matches ✓

So `. +?` grows to consume everything because `$` forces it to reach end. This explains why `{:<}` captures `hello world`.
